Two real bugs caught by the tests during T9, both fixed in the new file rather than papered over. (1) largestFrameCluster ranged over [][]protocol.BlockPos and appended to the ranged copy, so every group stayed one cell long and the bot would have clicked one frame of twelve; fixed by indexing. (2) endPortalInteriorCell originally looked for a hole in the ring's bounding box, which finds nothing on an ACTIVATED portal because Bedrock replaces the frames with end_portal blocks and there is no empty cell left — so enterendportal would have failed on every working portal. Rewritten to pick the most-enclosed cell of the structure, preferring filled cells then nearest, which identifies the middle of the ring in both states and in all three orientations without assuming a layout.

evidence.description: Primary-source review of DimsumMentAI autonomy stack confirming the specific behavioural gaps: agi/runner.go:208 (idle falls through to maybeWander), runner.go:218-228 (ActivityRest is a log line, ActivityApproach calls Wander), runner.go:563 (uncancellable context.Background wander goroutine), survival/manager.go:109-112 (Tick drives only auto-eat + auto-armor, so SleepInBed/AutoPlaceTorches/BuildEmergencyShelter/RecoverFromDeath/UseHealingPotion never fire proactively), survival/actions.go:284,298 and combat/shield_bow.go:179 (fixed blocking time.Sleep with zero variance), perception/visible_blocks.go:67-70 (perception scans a full axis-aligned cube with no FOV cone), jev/questions.go:24-30 (5-option activity menu), agi/brain.go:33-45 (Snapshot lacks time-of-day, light level, tool durability, inventory fullness).

External research gathered: mineflayer-movement README (raycast FOV steering with distance/danger/proximity/conformity heuristics, fov=240/rotations=15/blend=1); mindcraft-ce README ("standard robotic movement" criticism, door/gate/swim upgrades); zenn.dev first-hand build log (deterministic Executor beats LLM freedom; reverse tech-tree priority ordering; 1x1 shafts trip invalid_player_movement, use staircase mining; pathfinder.stop() leaves server-side desync; 2/3 reliability at stone tier, 0/3 at iron); Generative Agents (memory retrieval = recency+importance+relevance, reflection threshold 150, ~2-3x/day, full arch most believable); gophertunnel PlayerAuthInput docs (client sends once every tick, server-authoritative movement); Minecraft Wiki (walk 4.317 m/s, sprint 5.612 m/s, jump 1.2522 blocks; creeper 30-tick/1.5s fuse, triggers within 3 blocks, requires uninterrupted LOS, no idle/step sounds); bedrock.dev detection systems; Mineflayer issue #3899 anti-cheat false positives.

evidence.description: M1 (mode switch) + M2 (plan substrate) complete. Added internal/bot/agi/planner.go: ParsePlanReply (pure, tolerant of fences/prose/think blocks, drops unimplementable kinds, clamps to PlanMaxSteps), StepAction (kind -> action label:param table, rest/wait resolve to a real no-op), normalizeStepKind alias table, planningTick (expire -> replan-if-due -> wander-fallback -> failed-step-to-planner -> dispatch), requestPlan (async goroutine via AiClient.AskPlanner, single-flight + 30s cooldown), dispatchStep (one step in flight, retry once then hand back to planner), arrivedAt (post-move position check for coordinate go_to), announce (routes through the existing P4 speech gate). Wired cfg.Mode == config.ModePlanning into Tick below the reflex layer. Fixed a real config bug: applyAGIDefaults only handled an empty mode, so mode: "plan" was stored raw and NormalizeMode was never called at load time. configs/bot.yaml documents mode + plan budget in Indonesian with honest limitations.

Full validation suite green: go build ./... (exit 0), go vet ./... (no output), go test ./... (all 35 packages ok, 0 failures), go run ./cmd/pnxcheck (exit 0, every PNX login check passes). gofmt -l clean on internal/bot/agi, internal/config, tests/config. Also verified the real configs/bot.yaml loads through config.Load and yields mode="default" lifetime=60 replan=10 maxsteps=12. New tests: 12 in internal/bot/agi/planner_test.go (parse tolerance, rejection, clamping, kind normalisation, StepAction table, plan lifecycle, abandon, replan schedule, renderPlan, mode normalization) and 2 in tests/config/loader_test.go (planning off by default, aliases read from YAML).

Closed the two "not playing like a player" gaps found by code audit. (1) Block interaction could reach through walls: internal/bot/interact/visibility.go adds lineOfSightToBlock + onlyVisible with a see-through block table (torches, rails, water, crops, wall furniture), wired into Resolve's scanBlocks closure so BOTH the named path and the in-front path get it and cannot drift apart. Rule mirrors the storage layer exactly: target cell never occludes itself, unloaded cells never block, loaded cells block unless known see-through. Unknown blocks count as solid, so a new wall material occludes the moment it exists. (2) Building auto-digged any solid block: clearObstructions now returns bool and refuses storage + interactive blocks, reusing the existing storage.IsContainerBlock (suffix-matching, catches modded vaults) and interact.IsInteractiveBlockName rather than a third list. PlaceBlockAt aborts instead of building into a preserved cell. Added GetBlockName to common.BotInterface (*bot.Bot already satisfied it; no test fakes implement that interface).

Validation after both fixes: go build ./... exit 0, go vet ./... clean, go test ./... all packages ok with zero failures (12 new tests: 6 in internal/bot/interact/visibility_test.go covering wall rejection, fallback-to-visible-target, see-through non-occlusion, target-not-own-occluder, unknown-cells-pass, onlyVisible; 4 in internal/bot/building/placer/helpers_test.go covering 12 protected block names, ordinary terrain still dug, empty site, unnamed block). All 9 pre-existing interact tests and the rest of the suite still pass. go run ./cmd/pnxcheck exit 0. gofmt -l clean on every file touched; the files it does list are pre-existing CRLF files unrelated to this work and were deliberately left alone.

M3 safety reflexes. (1) Ground safety: new internal/bot/pathfinder/safety.go defines a lethal-block vocabulary (lava/fire/magma/campfire/cactus/berry bush/cobweb/wither rose/powder snow/end portal) plus the void (below -64 / above 320), and folds BOTH into IsHazard — so every existing neighbour rule (walk, drop, parkour, step-jump, diagonal, scaffold, ladder) inherits the safety without any of them knowing the list exists. Unloaded cells deliberately do not block, otherwise the bot roots itself in undecoded chunks. (2) Corner safety: appendCornerParkourIfPossible tested only a single arc midpoint, so a 2-block lateral swing could pass through a wall; replaced with cornerArcClear which walks the whole swept arc at feet+head height. (3) Breath safety: new ReflexSurface checked FIRST in DecideReflex, ahead of the health branch, because health only falls once air is nearly gone. Snapshot gains Underwater/SecondsUnderwater derived from the world (HeadCell = feet+1) rather than an air packet, since this client has never been shown receiving one; the clock resets on surfacing so ducking back down does not buy a fresh supply. surface() navigates via the pathfinder rather than reaching into the movement input loop, which rebuilds jump state every tick. New config knob low_air_seconds (default 10).

M3 validation: go build ./... exit 0, go vet ./... clean, go test ./... zero failures. 15 new tests. pathfinder/safety_test.go (8): lethal blocks are hazards, ordinary terrain is not (guards against the safety list swallowing the world), the void is a hazard with no block to name, unloaded cells are not hazards, HeadCell is one block up, water is water, corner arc needs the whole way clear (both directions). agi/curriculum_test.go (4 + 1 table): drowning outranks hunger AND an approaching player, the reflex waits for the threshold rather than firing on contact, dry land never triggers it even with a stale counter, and every pre-existing reflex is still reachable after the early return. Two real bugs were caught by these tests and fixed: cornerArcClear never took the absolute value of dz, so a straight +Z sweep had span 1 and checked a single cell; and the test fake initially returned names from GetBlockRID, which is a path the production bot never takes (it resolves names through WorldCache.BlockName(rid)).

M4 multi-dimension. New pure package internal/bot/dimension with: Dimension type (Unknown/Overworld/Nether/TheEnd, Unknown is a supported state not a failure), FromServerID mapping the three fixed Bedrock LevelChunk IDs and returning Unknown for anything else rather than guessing, Detect() inferring dimension from block names by MAJORITY of markers (so one netherrack decoration does not move the bot's map, and obsidian is deliberately in neither set because it is both the Nether portal frame and the End's floor), Classify() separating a lit portal from an unlit obsidian frame from end portal frames from an active end portal, and IsStrongholdHint reporting-only detection. Two real bugs fixed on the way: (1) WorldCache.Reset() and the local world model were never called on a dimension change, so the bot reasoned about a cache full of the world it had just left — now compared against the previous ChunkDimension on every LevelChunk, with a log line saying which way it went; (2) added LocalWorldModel.Reset() which drops mined/placed/hazard/temp/body-clearance overrides but deliberately KEEPS the chunk querier and path bounds, since those are where to ask and what the current trip is, not facts about a world.

M5 combat craft. (1) Weapon choice was a static tier list with no situational input, so a bot with a bow and a sword picked the sword against a creeper forty blocks away. New internal/bot/combat/choice.go splits that list by KIND first (sword/axe/bow/crossbow/trident/shield) and only then by tier within the kind, with overrides in order of how situational they are: water -> trident (a bow cannot be drawn and a melee swing may not connect); range with arrows -> crossbow then bow (a crossbow is not re-drawn between shots); two or more hostiles in melee -> axe (sweep clears the group where a sword takes them one at a time); otherwise sword. Falls back rather than giving up when the chosen kind is not carried, and WeaponNone is a real answer so fists still count. Slots are walked in index order so a tie is deterministic. (2) Shield: RaiseShield existed, was wired to nothing, and a shieldUp field was written and never read. PlanShield now distinguishes Raise (something in melee range, healthy enough to afford the seconds) / Lower (threat gone, or the bot is committed to the kill and blocking is a slower death) / Hold, and applyShield runs it every combat tick. (3) Durability: new shared internal/bot/durability package counting tool uses per slot, replacing at 80% of the vanilla limit. Wired into combat (every swing records a use) and into gathering's equipToolByType, which now skips a nearly-spent tool in favour of the next tier down — that was the named M5 failure: mining a stone vein with a wooden pickaxe until it breaks mid-swing, every block after coming out as nothing, while the gather still reports success. The tracker hangs off the bot behind an optional DurabilityTracker() method so both subsystems share one life per tool.

M6 inventory robustness. Two real bugs fixed. (1) sendStackRequest deleted its pendingCrafts entry on write failure and on connection close but NOT on the 5s timeout — every timed-out request left a map entry holding a channel nobody would read, for the rest of the session, and a late server response still found a listener for a craft path that had already given up. (2) FindItemSlotByName ranged over the inventory map, and Go randomises map iteration, so the same request could return a different slot each call for a bot holding two of something. That is the ghost-item bug the codebase already guards against elsewhere (dropTargetSlotLocked has a comment about exactly this): drop one stack, the server updates that slot, the other is still there, the next drop takes it too. Now a linear scan of slots 0-35. (3) New internal/bot/inventory/recovery.go: the diagnosis and recovery policy that did not exist. Container sessions tracked what the server last said but nothing noticed when the bot's view drifted from it, and nothing swept a stuck cursor back into the bag except a craft that had already failed. Diagnose/Plan fix ONE problem at a time in a fixed order (cursor, stale container, count drift) because inventory operations interfere — a resync issued with a cursor still attached reports a view the bot cannot act on. MergeConfirmed treats a non-nil confirmation as a COMPLETE snapshot and defers to the server on every count, dropping slots the server emptied.

M7 evidence logging. New leaf package internal/evidence (imports stdlib only, so it cannot cycle and passes archcheck): NDJSON events.jsonl, one object per line, with a UTC timestamp, a monotonic sequence number (wall clocks are not precise enough to order events that share a millisecond), a kind string, a human-readable detail, and free-form fields. Three rules in priority order: (1) never block the caller — a single non-blocking channel send, because a bot that stalls waiting for a log write is a bot that stood still at the wrong moment; (2) never rate-limit — the existing debuglog drops anything within 250ms, which is right for debugging one thing and exactly wrong for evidence, since the dropped line is the one you wanted; (3) never lie about gaps — a full buffer drops and COUNTS, and Summary() reports it at shutdown, so "the bot did not do this" stays distinguishable from "we did not see it happen". Rotates at 16MiB by rename, not truncate, because the session that went wrong is usually not the one you are watching when you notice. Wired to the plan lifecycle (plan ready / step start-adjacent / step done carrying the planner's own description / step retry / step failed with the replan flag / plan complete), reflexes (recorded BEFORE the action, so "the reflex fired" and "the reflex did what it should" stay distinct claims), and dimension changes. Added ReflexKind.String() because a reflex identifiable only by integer value cannot be looked up in a past session.

M7 validation plus final goal sweep. go build ./... exit 0, go vet ./... clean, go test ./... zero failures, go run ./cmd/pnxcheck exit 0, and go run ./cmd/archcheck reports 0 architecture findings. 9 new evidence tests, which caught three real defects in my own first draft: Record() contained a BLOCKING send followed by a select/default that could never help, directly contradicting the never-block promise; the sequence number was assigned at call time (racy across the eight goroutines that record) rather than at write time; and three tests read the file before Close(), which is a race, and two asserted full record counts through a 256-slot buffer where drops are correct behaviour. The evidence logger itself caught a test that "proved" a bot must not block on an unopenable log by using a path that MkdirAll could in fact create.

evidence.description: N1+N2+N5 done, plus a real bug caught by the new idle code. N1 Episode (internal/bot/agi/episode.go): Episode{Number,Title,Objective,StartedAt,EndsAt} with a HARD deadline — Remaining never negative, Over() true AT the deadline (not one nanosecond after), Urgency that is flat zero across the first 40% and then climbs, WrappingUp at 0.75 which is the "shoot" moment, and Describe() that carries the remaining time because every caller needs the budget and would otherwise re-derive it. ParseEpisode accepts "/episode 1 24m build a house", no slash, /ep alias, "m30" unit-first, "1h30m", "1h 30m" split by a space, and a bare number as minutes. N2 natural mode wired into Tick below the reflex layer, with the rule that a human outranks the schedule: Suspend() pauses work but NOT the episode clock (the recording is still going whether anyone is talking or not), lapsing after 90s, and it delegates to the SAME playAlong path the default brain uses rather than implementing a second personality. A new brief throws away the old plan outright. N5 idle: idle_alive vs idle_still chosen by a pure ChooseIdle(seed, bias) so a run cannot pick one mode every time, still idles get a longer window, and the rest period is HELD on the runner rather than re-derived from the clock each tick — a duration recomputed from the clock slides forward forever and the bot never wakes up. New config idle_still_bias, clamped not rejected.

Validation: go build ./... exit 0, go vet ./... clean, go test ./... zero failures, go run ./cmd/pnxcheck exit 0. 17 new tests (9 episode, 8 natural/idle). The idle tests caught a real self-deadlock I introduced while writing them: idle() held r.mu and then called planIdle(), which takes r.mu itself — the identical non-reentrant pattern that wedged Observe() and that the tests/agi/observe_test.go guard now exists to catch. It hung the package for the full 60s test timeout before failing, which is exactly the signature of that bug. Also required giving Runner a log()/note() pair that tolerate a nil bot: the agi package's own tests run in-package and cannot construct a *bot.Bot because the bot imports agi, so every notifying method has to survive a runner with no bot or the decision layer becomes untestable.

N4 discovery + N3 Jev as primary controller. N4: internal/bot/agi/discovery.go — Vocabulary built from what the bot has actually SEEN, replacing the hardcoded survival list (oak_log/chest/bed/night) that cannot work on an addon server and is entirely empty on a one-block world. Names normalised (namespace, case, spaces) so one block is not three terms, air excluded so the list is not topped by "air", most-seen first because a block seen once is scenery and seen forty times is a resource, stable ordering so a reshuffle is not mistaken for a discovery, capped at 48 so the state text stays inside the model's budget. Wired into Observe() and into describeState so BOTH the fast and slow models see what this world is made of. N3: a new Jev question jev.needs_the_big_brain, asked in the same parallel pass rather than as a second round trip, with a deliberately high 0.75 threshold because the big model is the expensive tier and a bot that thinks every few seconds reads as laggy rather than thoughtful. WantsBigBrain refuses to escalate on a judgement that never arrived — a missing answer must never read as a confident yes, or a session with Jev down spends the expensive tier every tick. The escalation prompt deliberately is NOT a task list, and says so. And the standing gap is closed: buildDecisionPrompt now carries plan, goal, world contents, episode clock and visible mobs, with the instruction to follow the plan and not to invent actions the world cannot support.

N6 watchdog + N7 oneblock, completing all seven layers. N6 internal/bot/agi/watchdog.go: Diagnose returns ONE fault in a fixed order — disconnect first (nothing else can be tried until the connection is back), then death (a dead bot is also a motionless one, so checking stillness first means unsticking a corpse), then stuck. Death and disconnect act on the FIRST sighting because waiting to confirm a dead bot means lying on the respawn screen for another tick; stuck needs two consecutive agreeing readings because one tick can be a server hiccup and a watchdog that thrashes gets switched off. Exploring is exempt from the stuck check — a bot walking somewhere on purpose is supposed to leave its position alone, and calling that stuck produces a bot that interrupts its own journey every thirty seconds. PositionChanged beats a pure clock because a server applying a freeze still answers ticks. N7 internal/bot/agi/oneblock.go: DetectOneBlock is a CONFIDENCE not a boolean, because "one block in reach" is also "a small room" and a sweep of identical floor tiles looks identical; ConfirmOneBlock takes the second opinion after standing still, which is the difference between a room and a single-block world. Air is excluded so a bot on a hillside does not look like one. OneBlockPlan states the one verb there is — break the block, see what turned up, build upward — and rules out what is absent without instructing the bot to go find it.

evidence.description: Table craft: AutoCraftRecipeStackRequestAction replaced by the staged-grid path (Take -> Place -> CraftRecipe -> CraftResults -> Consume per staged slot -> Place) with slots 32..40. New tests: internal/bot/inventory_table_craft_test.go (grid mapping, consume-per-slot action order, unsupported-recipe rejection) and internal/bot/inventory/crafting/table_test.go (arm watch before click, fail when no ContainerOpen, close by the assigned window ID).

A* recalculation loop: WalkTo no longer re-plans for a re-asserted destination. shouldReplanForWalkTo is pure and unit-tested in internal/bot/walk_to_replan_test.go (same target reuses route, sub-0.25 drift reuses, moved target re-plans, no-route / changed mode always re-plans). Fixes both the "recalculating path using A*" every 250ms for a one-block drop and the stuck-ladder reset that prevented escalation.

Break animation and sound: one shared rhythm in internal/bot/movement/animation/rhythm.go (WindUp/Cadence/JitteredAim/Beats), now used by the chopper, the miner, the obstruction clear and the obstacle unstick (which had its own fixed 300ms metronome). Beats refuses to end on a runt swing - the new TestBeatsNeverEndOnARuntSwing caught a real 86ms final swing that would have shown as the exact arm vibration the rhythm exists to prevent. Tests: rhythm_test.go, break_obstacle_test.go, chop_rhythm_test.go.

AGI watchdog self-deadlock found while running the goal validation gate: watch() took r.mu across the reading and then took it again to count the repeat, and sync.Mutex is not reentrant, so the loop wedged on its first tick (this is why the bot still needed chat commands to act). Split into observePosition and recordFault, each locking once. Regression test internal/bot/agi/watchdog_lock_test.go runs it on a goroutine with a timeout.
